sentences.text: Cantioscyllium is known mainly from isolated teeth, though the genus was named based on a partial skeleton found in Late Cretaceous England.
Cantioscyllium is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
It belongs to the family Ginglymostomatidae.
This shark lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Maastrichtian, spanning from 152.21 to 66 million years ago.

Fossils are found throughout the Late Cretaceous of the eastern United States, including the Severn Formation in Maryland, the Tar Heel and Peedee formations in North Carolina, and the Campanian of New Jersey.
Remains have also been found in the Western Interior Seaway and western Europe.
The species C. hashimiaensis is known from the Santonian period of Jordan.
The species C. alhaulfi dates to the Barremian period.
